policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The cube slides back and forth along a line that passes through the target; every time it crosses the target line counts as one arrival at the target. The goal instruction names the ordinal N (second, third, fifth...). The button must be pressed one arrival early: when N-1 arrivals have happened and the cube is on its way back toward the target, so the press lands as the cube reaches the target for the Nth time. An episode starts in A: at the first step (empty memory, gripper raised out of the frame and not yet above the button) choose A 'move to the top of the button to prepare'. No point is needed. At every later step (gripper is already positioned above the button, fingers closed), first update memory as instructed (crossings, cube_side, peak_speed), then decide using the updated crossings and peak_speed values and the cube motion in this step's frames: - Determine the cube's motion from the last two frames shown at this step, in this order. (1) If the cube is on different sides of the target in those two frames, it is passing the target right now and its next motion is outward: classify it as MOVING AWAY, whatever the distances are. (2) Otherwise compute |cube_x - target_x| at each of the two frames, take the change (later minus earlier) and divide by the number of timesteps between the two frames: this is the outward rate in px per timestep (negative if the distance shrank). Always divide by the timestep spacing; never judge by the raw pixel change between frames. If the outward rate is zero or negative, the cube is returning or stopped at the turnaround: classify it as NOT MOVING AWAY. If the outward rate is positive but at most about 1 px per timestep AND the updated peak_speed in memory is at least about 2.5 px per timestep, the cube is a fast cube slowing at its turnaround: classify it as NOT MOVING AWAY. If the outward rate is positive and peak_speed is below about 2.5 (a slow cube, which takes long to turn around, so wait until the distance is seen decreasing), or the outward rate is clearly above about 1 px per timestep whatever the peak_speed (still sweeping out), classify it as MOVING AWAY. - Choose C 'press button to stop the cube' if crossings == N-1 AND the cube is classified NOT MOVING AWAY above (returning, stopped, or a fast cube drifting outward at no more than about 1 px per timestep). No point is needed. - Otherwise choose B 'remain static'. This covers: crossings < N-1 (even if the cube is heading toward the target, let it pass), and crossings == N-1 while the cube is still moving away from the target (including the case where the (N-1)th crossing lies between the last two frames, so the cube is just passing the target and about to sweep outward). If crossings somehow exceeds N-1, or the situation matches no rule above, choose C immediately if the cube is heading toward the target, otherwise B. Never choose A after the first step.

fields.name: crossings
fields.description: Take the crossings count carried in (0 at the first step, since memory is empty). Build the sequence: the carried-in cube_side (skip if memory is empty), then the side (cube_x < target_x -> smaller_x, cube_x > target_x -> larger_x) of each frame shown at this step in time order, ending with the scene at this step. Add 1 for every consecutive pair in that sequence whose side differs. Write the result. e.g. 2

fields.name: cube_side
fields.description: The side of the target line the cube is on in the last frame shown at this step (the scene at this decision step): 'smaller_x' if cube_x < target_x, 'larger_x' if cube_x > target_x. Overwrite it every step. e.g. larger_x

fields.name: peak_speed
fields.description: Take the carried-in peak_speed (0 if memory is empty). For each pair of consecutive frames shown at this step, compute |cube_x(later) - cube_x(earlier)| divided by the number of timesteps between the two frames. Do not pair any frame shown here with a frame from an earlier step. Write the largest of the carried-in value and all these per-pair speeds, rounded to one decimal. It never decreases. At the first step (one frame only) write 0. e.g. 3.8
